en: The First Application of Meditation: At one time, the Blessed Bodhisattva was at Urubilvā.
Dwelling at the foot of the Bodhi tree on the bank of the river Nairañjanā, he remained established in imperturbability regarding the factors conducive to awakening.
He dwells devoted to the practice of meditation regarding the [four] foundations of mindfulness.
2. During the first watch of the night...
In the supernormal knowledge of the realization of the sphere of psychic power, he directs his mind toward various kinds of psychic powers.
(He experiences the range of supernormal power: having been one, he becomes many;
having been many, he becomes one.
He becomes visible; he also experiences disappearance through his knowledge and vision. [Even] behind a wall...
He goes unhindered even through walls and through mountains, just as if through space; he walks upon the earth...
For example, he walks upon water without becoming wet,
just as if it were the great earth; and even in the sky, [he walks].
He strides with the paryanka-gait,
just like a winged bird; even these two,
the moon and the sun, [he traverses] in this manner.
Hardhika and Mahāhardhika, possessing such great majesty,
stroked and rubbed [the earth] with their hands,
even as far as the Brahma-world with their bodies.
"Bring [it] under control.
Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva,
dwelt at Uruvilvā.
On the bank of the Nairañjanā river, standing at the foot of the Bodhi tree,
he attained imperturbability regarding the factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣika-dharma*).
Dwelling devoted to the yoga of the forest, during the first watch of the night,
[he experiences] manifold spheres of supernormal power.
[He] experiences [it].
(Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva,) while dwelling at Uruvilvā...
Just as before, he dwells [there] as long as he is questioned;
during the first watch of the night...
He directs his mind toward the supernormal knowledge that realizes the recollection of past lives; he [perceives] it in its many forms.
He recollects his past lives;
for example, one birth among the gods.
He recollects four eons of dissolution, and even many eons of dissolution.
8. Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, while dwelling at Uruvilvā, remained at the foot of the Bodhi tree on the bank of the river Nairañjanā.
Having attained imperturbability, he dwells devoted to the practice of cultivation regarding the factors conducive to awakening throughout the night.
In the first watch [of the night], he recollects his former abodes.
Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva—
Dwelling at Urubilvā, as before,
he dwelt devotedly [to his practice] until the middle of the night.
He directs his mind toward the supernormal knowledge that realizes the divine ear. By means of the divine ear—
With the purified divine ear, which transcends that of humans, he hears both kinds of sounds: those of humans and those of non-humans.
"and those who are far away or those who are near.
(Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva,) while dwelling at Uruvilvā—
On the bank of the Nairañjanā,
standing at the foot of the Bodhi tree,
he attained imperturbability regarding the factors conducive to awakening.
While dwelling devoted to the practice of forest yoga,
during the middle watch of the night,
he [attained] the knowledge of the divine ear.
experiences.
